title: User-Centric Metrics
description: Master Core Web Vitals, INP, LCP, and CLS: what they measure, how to instrument them in the field, and how to improve them with targeted optimizations.

data.text: User-centric metrics measure what real people experience: how fast content appears, how quickly the page responds to taps and keystrokes, and whether the page shifts while they are reading. Google's Core Web Vitals — LCP, INP, and CLS — are now ranking signals in search and direct measures of user satisfaction.

Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures loading performance. Interaction to Next Paint (INP) measures responsiveness. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measures visual stability. Together they cover the three pillars of page experience: speed, responsiveness, and stability.

LCP measures when the largest text or image element becomes visible. Common LCP candidates are hero images, large headings, and video posters. Optimize LCP by reducing server response time, using preload for critical resources, and removing render-blocking scripts.

data.title: LCP Optimization Patterns

data.text: INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in 2024. It measures the latency of all interactions across the page session, reporting the worst near-miss. INP values come from Event Timing entries, and you can observe them with the PerformanceObserver.

data.title: Observing and Improving INP
data.content: Measure interaction latency and reduce it.

data.text: CLS sums the impact of every unexpected layout shift. Shifts caused by user interaction within 500 ms are excluded. Common causes are images without dimensions, dynamically injected ads, and web fonts flashing in after text has already rendered.

data.title: CLS Fixes
data.content: Prevent layout shifts from common culprits.

data.text: The web-vitals library provides reliable field measurement of Core Web Vitals. It handles browser differences, bfcache restores, and visibility changes. Report metrics to your analytics backend to track trends over time.

data.title: Production RUM with web-vitals
data.content: Send Core Web Vitals to analytics.

data.title: Field Data Differs from Lab Data
data.text: Lighthouse scores on fast hardware are not representative. Always validate optimizations against real-user data from CrUX or your own RUM pipeline. A 'good' Lighthouse score can still mask poor field performance on 3G or low-end devices.

terms.definition: A set of user-centric metrics (LCP, INP, CLS) that measure loading, interactivity, and visual stability.
When the largest visible text or image element finishes rendering.
The latency of the slowest interaction during a page session.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Core Web Vitals measure real user experience: LCP, INP, CLS
LCP targets the largest visible element; optimize with preloads and reduced render-blocking
INP measures the worst interaction latency across the page session
CLS penalizes unexpected layout shifts; reserve space for images, ads, and fonts
Use web-vitals in production for reliable field measurement
Validate lab optimizations against field data; they often differ
data.takeaway: Core Web Vitals connect performance work to business outcomes. Measure them in production, set realistic budgets, and use attribution data to fix the root cause of each poor metric.
